title: The login that kept the old session
blurb: Elevation reused the session id and trusted the body's device label.
prompt: A security review found that the session endpoint hands back the same session id it was given, so a pre-login id becomes authenticated after elevation. The same handler takes the device class from the request body and creates a session for a caller that never completed the auth flow. Review it, fix it, and prove the id changes on elevation.
aiNote: The draft reuses the incoming X-Session-Id instead of minting a new one, so a planted pre-login id is authenticated after login; it stores the device_class from the request body rather than the validated claims; and it creates a session without checking that the auth assertion completed.
testIdea: Post a request with a planted X-Session-Id and assert the response carries a different id and the old id no longer authenticates; send device_class in the body and assert the stored class is the one from the claims; post without an auth assertion and expect 401.
followUps: What is the difference between a session id and an identity?
Where does the device class have to come from so a caller cannot forge it?
What should happen to a request that arrives with an old session id mid-flight?
